# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: THE DUKE DECIDES (Headon Hill, 1903/1904, A. Wessels Co.)

**Ch I – The Man with the Mandate.** Six p.m., May, uptown Broadway NYC. Dry-goods store employees leave via basement (timekeeper, private detective). Protagonist: **Charles Hanbury**, ex-subaltern, English cavalry, ruined by extravagance; lamed by fall down hatchway on voyage out; now adds columns for a dry-goods store, $8/week, $5 to boarding-house keeper. Walks home via Bowery to Brooklyn bridge. Stout fair Englishman in light frock-coat and Panama hat, Cockney accent, calls himself **Jevons**; takes him to basement saloon. Offers job: planting faked US Treasury bonds on Bank of England, £3 million. Shows five $100 notes. Threat: life worthless if he deserts. Contact: **Mr. Clinton Ziegler, Hotel Cecil, London**. Ship: **St. Paul**, sailing for Southampton "day after tomorrow". Telegram in boarding-house: uncle and cousin killed in railway accident; from solicitors **Pattisons**; £1000 cabled to Morgan's. Hanbury is now **Charles Augustus Trevor Fitzroy Hanbury, seventh Duke of Beaumanoir**, rent-roll £200,000/yr.

**Ch II – On Board the St. Paul.** Hanbury books as plain Charles Hanbury. Plans to visit Ziegler first. Meets **Leonie Sherman** (American, dainty), mother Mrs. Sherman (wants her to marry English duke—Leonie finds it tiresome). Father **Senator Leonidas Sherman** (Washington, detained). Friends in London: 140 Grosvenor Gardens. Fifth day, off Irish coast: Leonie warns him of man in brown covert-coat and tweed cap smoking cigar in holder, **Marker**, who shadows him. Marker's cabin next door.

**Ch III – A Task-master in Goggles.** Southampton; boat-train to Waterloo. Mrs. Sherman invites him to 140 Grosvenor Gardens. Marker follows in cab to Hotel Cecil. Hanbury gives name Hanbury. Meets Ziegler: old, invalid chair, snowy beard, purple puffy cheeks, blue glasses, piping treble. Three masked men attack; Ziegler orders chloroform, then spares him ("lied to me"). Ziegler knows of Leonie: agent (steward) seated him next to her. Real bonds carried by Senator Sherman. Instructions: cultivate Sherman women; return to Ziegler **Saturday noon, three days hence**.

**Ch IV – The Lady in the Landau.** Top of staircase: **Alec Forsyth** (Eton friend, Foreign Office third-grade clerk, £230/yr), visiting **Mrs. Talmage Eglinton** (Cecil, next suite to Ziegler's). Strand restaurant lunch. Deaths: late Duke and nephew **George Hanbury** in collision on racing special to Newmarket; double funeral at **Prior's Tarrant** (Hertfordshire seat); cousin **Sybil Hanbury** (18) living at Beaumanoir House, Piccadilly. Forsyth loves Sybil. Sadgroves (**General Sadgrove**, late Indian Staff Corps, C.B., wife **Mrs. Sadgrove/Madge**) now at 140 Grosvenor Gardens. Duke offers Forsyth secretary post (£800 rising to £2000; dower-house). Mrs. Talmage Eglinton in landau (driver Bennett) invites Duke to tea Saturday at Cecil; Duke refuses, says he goes to Prior's Tarrant. Duke resolves to be "a man not a cur."

**Ch V – Ziegler Begins to Move.** Sunday at Prior's Tarrant. Forsyth's letter: met Shermans at General's dinner; did not go to tea. Duke at church; vicar **Mr. Bristow** (wife Mrs. Bristow). Third gardener **Jennings** lassoed in park copse. Butler **Manson**. Night: state bedroom ("Duke's Room"); charcoal brazier lowered down chimney; Duke awakens, escapes.

**Ch VI – The General is Curious.** Tea at Grosvenor Gardens: Mrs. Sadgrove, Mrs. Sherman, Leonie, Sybil. Mrs. Talmage Eglinton visits; General recognizes her landau had knocked down a man in Buckingham Palace Road (the Duke). Duke arrives with black silk sling, diachylon on wrist. Duke probes about Senator's bonds, warns of "sharps". General notes "vibration in the moral atmosphere."

**Ch VII – The Men on the Stairs.** Forsyth's rooms, John Street, Adelphi. Duke hides there; tells of attempts. Marker at door with bogus chemist's story. Forsyth goes to Constitutional Club; returns to find door forced; Duke gone. Two men on stairs: gaunt man in clerical garb, burly man in shabby tweeds and bowler hat.

**Ch VIII – The Cut Panel.** Sybil alone in white drawing-room, Beaumanoir House. Butler **Prince**. "Inspector Chantrey, CID" (fake, clerical garb) calls; sent away by Duke. Duke stays overnight; Sybil and Forsyth. Night: Sybil hears sawing on Duke's door; grabs intruder in tweeds; Duke with Smith & Wesson takes intruder out. Panel cut with watch-spring saw.

**Ch IX – The Strategy of the General.** General visits Duke; plan: go to Prior's Tarrant with house-party (Shermans, Sadgroves, Forsyth, Sybil). Pathan servant **Azimoolah Khan**. Apple-woman under Green Park railings watched; footman Steptoe. Duke invited Shermans.

**Ch X – A Duty Call.** General checks Scotland Yard (no Inspector Chantrey). Invites Mrs. Talmage Eglinton; visits Hotel Cecil. Learns Ziegler is next suite. Azimoolah (disguised as Thakore of Bhurtnagur) raids Ziegler's suite; hubbub. Mrs. Talmage Eglinton asks when Duke leaves: "8.45 from St. Pancras" told.

**Ch XI – On the Terrace.** Train derailed (timber across rails) between St. Albans and Harpenden; Duke not in carriage. Forsyth received forged telegram (from "Sybil Hanbury") and returned to Beaumanoir House. General deduces Mrs. Talmage Eglinton = Ziegler's partner. Fight on terrace: General and Forsyth seize Azimoolah by mistake.

**Ch XII – The Man Under the Seat.** Duke on 8.45 train; Marker under seat; Duke drags him out; Marker shows ticket at Radlett, leaves. Obstruction at Elstree-area upline; Duke escapes into wood; keeper's cottage.

**Ch XIII – At the Keeper's Cottage.** Keeper **Mayne** (old, sons gone); Sir Claude Asprey's coverts. Fake "Colonel Anstruther Walcot, 14th Dragoon Guards" (American). Duke escapes out window with £5 note for Mayne. Azimoolah follows him home; Duke attacks him on terrace.

**Ch XIV – Too Many Women.** Azimoolah is General's man. Anonymous letter with Mrs. Talmage Eglinton's perfume. Mrs. Talmage Eglinton accepts invitation. Sybil tells General "too many women"; partnership.

**Ch XV – A New Cure for Headache.** Mrs. Talmage Eglinton claims headache; French maid **Rosa**. General goes to London to see Ziegler. Mrs. Talmage Eglinton leaves at night via stile/dog-cart, Azimoolah follows. Letter to Ziegler posted.

**Ch XVI – A Delicate Mission.** Forsyth escorts Mrs. Talmage Eglinton to London; she goes to Bond Street. Forsyth sees Ziegler's suite (Benzon, "Leopold Benzon", fake Colonel). Ziegler gives sealed packet for Duke. Forsyth lunches with Mrs. Talmage Eglinton at Kettner's; declares "very far from being indifferent" to her.

**Ch XVII – Where is the Duke?** Senator due. Duke vanished at dawn; Azimoolah says Duke took train at Tring, then Bletchley junction, North of England express (to Liverpool). Mrs. Talmage Eglinton at library door.

**Ch XVIII – The Senator and the Securities.** Senator Leonidas Sherman on *Campania* at Liverpool; purser Mr. Seaton. Duke meets him, claims acquaintance. Corridor express to Prior's Tarrant. Senator deposits box in new safe in muniment room; Duke keeps key.

**Ch XIX – In the Crypt.** Night: Forsyth disguised as Duke (make-up) meets Ziegler and four men in crypt (Dutch garden door). Forsyth gives dummy package (tissue paper). Ziegler begs for bonds back; Forsyth refuses; Ziegler and men leave.

**Ch XX – In the Muniment Room.** Duke guards safe. Ziegler enters with Rosa (disguised: Ziegler = Cora Lestrade in wig). Duke captures Ziegler; Senator, General, Forsyth, Sybil arrive. Azimoolah captures Benzon through window. Reveal: "Mrs. Talmage Eglinton" = **Cora Lestrade**, American ex-convict, Sing Sing. General's explanation. Lestrade allowed to depart; Benzon escapes.

**Ch XXI – The Honor of the House.** Bonds at Bank of England. Duke confesses to Senator; Senator: "straight man." Six months later: Forsyth married Sybil in September; Duke and Duchess in Egypt. *Standard* report: Cora Lestrade stabbed on Vienna train. Ends.

---

## BOOK 2: THE SPRING SONG (Forrest Reid, 1916, Edward Arnold)

**Ch I – The Beginning of the Adventure.** June train. **Griffith (Grif) Weston**, 13, sensitive, sleepy-eyed, delicate health; sisters **Barbara** (12, prim), **Ann** (10, fat, freckled, mouth-breather), brother **Jim** (9, fidgety, riddles, sailor suit); **Edward** (15, school, fair, cocky, cigarettes; called "Angelina" at school) comes later. Miss Johnson (governess, pince-nez, writing novel *Be True, Fond Heart*). Parents abroad in East. Bulldog **Pouncer** (Ann says "Bouncer"). Aunt Caroline (Miss Annesley, tall, fair). Grandfather **Canon Annesley** (glebe house, writing book on fairies; organist **Mr. Clement Bradley**). Father specialist, mother. Miss Johnson's worries re Grif's health.

**Ch II – In the Lane.** Walk; Bradley met in lane (silver hair, ebony stick, sly eyes). Grif's room (window onto wood with whispering trees).

**Ch III – New Arrivals.** Edward arrives with **Palmer Dorset** (red crisp hair, freckles, reddish-brown eyes, sturdy; "Balmer"/"Palmer"; detective-minded, Sherlock Holmes posture). Riddle "Bun." Edward smokes. Canon: "Look not for whales in the Euxine sea." Miss Johnson's novel plot. Jim: "Angelina" heroine's name.

**Ch IV – At the Window.** Night. Grif hears wood-voices singing Spring Song; flute heard.

**Ch V – The Garden Door.** Croquet tournament (Jim, Ann, Palmer, Edward, Barbara; Mr. **Drummond**, curate). Grif wanders to wood, stream, garden door; meets **Captain Narcissus Batt** and sisters **Miss Nancy** and **Miss Jane**; tea under cedars; Billy Tremaine's room unseen.

**Ch VI – Music.** Church; Bradley plays "Spring Song" (Italian, by Gian Peruzzi); vision of old city. Grif sings scale; Bradley says he saw ghost (his pupil, dead) in church.

**Ch VII – Questions and Answers.** Supper; canon: Bradley Oxford man; Billy Tremaine (Batt's grandson, dead ~4 years, age ~Grif's). Miss Johnson suspects Grif untruthful.

**Ch VIII – Grey Weather.** Miss Johnson sees naked boy (Palmer) in river; Jim bitten by Pouncer-lion game. Palmer's play performed (*Be True Fond Heart* burlesque) in back drawing-room; Miss Johnson offended; Grif apologizes.

**Ch IX – Pouncer.** Circus passes. Pouncer stolen. Grif runs after circus, sleeps by stream.

**Ch X – Through the Darkness.** Grif finds circus camp at night; frees dogs; fights circus boy; sleeps in private estate wood.

**Ch XI – Inspector Dorset.** Palmer borrows bicycle and money; plans stakeout with Edward; Man with earrings (**George**, "Prairie Dick") caught in garden; Palmer shoots his leg with secondhand revolver from saddler's; canon confiscates it. Doctor **O'Neill** (bachelor, specialist, ~30s) admires Palmer.

**Ch XII – The Spring Song.** Grif dawn in wood; dragonfly; flute heard again.

**Ch XIII – The Perfumes of Arabia.** Grif home; visits church, reads Tobit; Billy Tremaine's grave ("William Batt Tremaine, aged fourteen"). Palmer runs off after spying on Bradley.

**Ch XIV – The Recognition.** Bradley: flute was dead boy's; warns Grif of danger from the dead; shadow-story.

**Ch XV – Danger.** Palmer discovers Bradley's real name Tennant. Grif sleepwalks at night, nearly fainting.

**Ch XVI – Grif Receives a Visitor.** Grif sends note via Jim; Bradley visits, tells shadow-murder story; Grif terrified.

**Ch XVII – Fantasy.** O'Neill: Grif worse; wants Pouncer back. Grif's dream: chimney dogs, graveyard gate, shadow strangling.

**Ch XVIII – Grif Awakens.** Pouncer saves him; three days ill (Monday to Wednesday).

**Ch XIX – Doctor O'Neill Calls in a Specialist.** O'Neill and Palmer in Jonah's Bower; plan to investigate Bradley. Palmer's theory: former asylum patient.

**Ch XX – Miss Johnson's Birthday.** Age-trick (34); bonfire stopped; Palmer summoned by O'Neill.

**Ch XXI – Palmer at Work.** O'Neill gives Palmer small revolver. They search Bradley's lodgings: signature torn, blotter; Bradley returns; Palmer's shadow remark; Palmer tells childhood Jane/sovereign story.

**Ch XXII – Fire!** Johnnie reports fire; Bradley burns church, plays organ; leaps from tower, dies. Canon dismissive; Aunt Caroline critical of Palmer.

**Ch XXIII – The Glittering Net.** Bradley's history: homicide, asylum, released; disguised name. Canon rebuilding fund. O'Neill argues against school for Grif; Aunt Caroline doubts Palmer's goodness. Grif lost, drawn to flute.

**Ch XXIV – Grif Falls Asleep.** End of September. Grif visits Miss Nancy; confides; she shows Billy's room; Grif falls asleep in her arms. Ends "THE END."
